key_insight: Cubic HUBO captures substantial third-order configurational energy contributions in lithium-rich oxyfluorides that quadratic QUBO models cannot represent.
engineering_relevance: Higher-order energy models could improve configurational modeling of disordered-rocksalt cathodes, provided magnetic-state dependence is accounted for.
method: Compute composition-preserving, fixed-geometry energy maps using spin-polarized DFT for LMOF and LMTiOF.
Compare quadratic QUBO and cubic HUBO fits and verify nonadditivity through direct DFT energy differences.
Compare magnetic initializations to assess dependence on the converged electronic state.
evidence_signal: Cubic HUBO substantially reduces fitting errors in both materials, while LMTiOF shows strong dependence of its third-order contribution on the converged electronic state.
watch_item: Extracted higher-order terms are effective couplings among composition-preserving exchange variables, not uniquely identified microscopic three-atom interactions.
paper_title: First-Principles Identification of Higher-Order Configurational Energy Terms and Their Magnetic-State Dependence in Lithium-Rich Oxyfluorides: From QUBO to HUBO
